outcome: Produce a calibrated, evidence-cited 0-100 composite score, letter grade, and 0-9 maturity stage for the stated target, using the fixed 8-dimension rubric and the matching domain module(s) -- never inflated by confident presentation and never defaulted to a mid-score where evidence is missing.
activation: User asks to rate, grade, score, or evaluate a project, pitch, codebase, research proposal, design, or personal skill-building goal
exclusions: Do not fabricate market data, user counts, test-coverage percentages, or competitor names
Do not treat a confident or detailed pitch as evidence of quality on its own
inputs_and_preconditions: A target is identified: current directory, pasted text, a file path, or two-plus targets for compare mode

hard_invariants.description: The stated 0-100 composite is arithmetically consistent with the stated per-dimension scores and the fixed rubric weights (10/15/10/15/20/15/10/5%).
A dimension with no real evidence either way is marked Unrated -- insufficient evidence, not silently defaulted to a mid-range score.

An A/S letter grade is not assigned unless the rationale cites actual outside validation (real users, real data, independent third-party review) -- not confident self-presentation or internal conviction alone.

A fluently written, detailed, jargon-correct pitch with no verifiable evidence behind its claims is not scored materially higher than an equally unevidenced but plainly written pitch making the same underlying claims.

When the target supplies concrete, specific outside validation (named user counts, independent reviews, third-party citations), the rating is not artificially suppressed to a low grade regardless of the skepticism default.

decision_points: Classify target class(es) before selecting domain modules
Choose quick vs full vs deep vs compare output mode
side_effects: Read repo/file contents actually named or supplied
Do not fetch outside context in default mode; WebSearch only in deep mode
validation: Composite arithmetic checked against stated per-dimension scores and fixed weights
Grade anchor matches the calibration rules in the rubric
Unrated is used where evidence is absent, not a guessed mid-score
failure_recovery: If asked to compare against a prior scorecard, diff directly instead of re-deriving from scratch
quality_heuristics: Most real early-stage work lands C/D
examples_and_calibration: A shallow but confidently-written pitch should score low on Evidence & Validation and Differentiation despite fluent prose
A real, tested, but externally-unvalidated small project should land C-range, not A
A target with genuine, specific outside validation should be able to reach A/S -- skepticism is a default, not a ceiling
